newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market routine, Cuba shipments eyed.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market routine, Cuba shipments eyed.

text.p: A couple of new orders emerged on the sugar freight market at the end of the week but business was generally routine, shipbrokers said on Friday. Market sources said there were a few teething problems at start of Cuba's 1996/97 cane sugar shipment cycle, which shipbrokers put down to the usual logistical problems getting the first cargoes to the ports. "It's been quite quiet on the whole," said one shipbroker.

Of the day's fresh inquiry, E D & F Man quoted for 12,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maceio to Manfredonia for the end of December and was said to be on subjects with 14,000 tonnes in bags from the same origin to Iran for December/January.
Alpine was open for 20/22,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Mediterranean/Black Sea for mid-January.

Firmer business included Mauritius Sugar Syndicate, which fixed 17,750/18,000 tonnes of bulk sugar on its usual run from Port Louis to London for end-December dates. The rate achieved for the fixture has yet to emerge.
Louis Dreyfus fixed its earlier order for 12/13,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to Colombo for early January.
Elsewhere, Syria tendered to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws for shipment in February, with the tender to be held on January 8.
